prompt:
Generate a landscape 16:10 illustration (1600x1000 px or larger) for a DIY car-repair guide. Oil drain: this is the engine oil drain plug, on a 2010 BMW 328i (E90), 3.0L inline-6. Step: "Drain the sump".
Look: clean realistic 3D technical illustration, light neutral studio background, matte materials, soft light and soft contact shadows, tight framing, minimal detail. Realism is for materials and light only: no invented detail, no orange or other saturated accent colours (copper parts may be copper).
View: End-on view straight along the axis of the part, on a small patch of plain simplified surface; no ground, horizon or body edges visible. Tight close-up: the hero fills about 40-60% of the frame. The hero and only a small patch of the surface it sits in form one isolated object floating on the plain light background; the patch ends well inside the frame and never reaches the left, right or bottom edge.
Show: HERO: The engine oil drain plug seen end-on: a short plain external hex head (17 mm size) with a flat copper-coloured crush washer under the head. Do NOT depict its orientation: keep it a plain generic shape. A thin flat copper-coloured crush washer sitting between the plug head and the oil pan surface.
Background only, simplified and dim: oil pan surface.
Leave out entirely: pan bolts and ribs, wrench or socket, hands, people, engine badges, logos, brand marks, licence plates.
Layout: plain empty light margin of at least 8% of the width on the left and right and 8% of the height at the bottom; nothing touches those edges, the subject floats on the plain ground. Keep the top 3%-17% of the height plain light background.
No text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, callout lines or watermarks anywhere. Anything not described above stays a plain generic shape; if unsure how a real part looks, leave it out.
